22	// The column widths, defaultColumns and calculateColumns used to live here.
23	// calculateColumns clamped Modified at 15 *after* handing it the remainder, so
24	// the columns overflowed the viewport by up to 34 at narrow widths — the shape
25	// datatable's TestTheWorkspacesLayoutFitsANarrowTerminal was written against.
26	// The widths are in columns.go now and the arithmetic is the solver's.
27	
28	// View renders the view
29	func (m Model) View() string {
30		// Mode input - show input form overlay
31		if m.mode == ModeAdding && m.input != nil {
32			return lipgloss.Place(
33				m.width, m.height,
34				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
35				m.input.View(),
36				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground),
37			)
38		}
39	
40		// Mode confirm - show confirm modal overlay
41		if m.mode == ModeConfirmingDelete && m.confirmModal != nil {
42			return lipgloss.Place(
43				m.width, m.height,
44				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
45				m.confirmModal.View(),
46				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground),
47			)
48		}
49	
50		// Mode scan-all - show the option modal overlay
51		if m.mode == ModeConfirmingScanAll && m.scanAllModal != nil {
52			return lipgloss.Place(
53				m.width, m.height,
54				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
55				m.scanAllModal.View(),
56				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground),
57			)
58		}
59	
60		// Mode renaming - show rename input overlay
61		if m.mode == ModeRenaming && m.input != nil {
62			return lipgloss.Place(
63				m.width, m.height,
64				lipgloss.Center, lipgloss.Center,
65				m.input.View(),
66				lipgloss.WithWhitespaceBackground(theme.ColorBackground),
67			)
68		}
69	
70		// Content style with left padding (for non-table states only)
71		contentStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).PaddingLeft(1)
72	
73		// Normal mode
74		if m.error != "" {
75			errorStyle := lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground).Foreground(theme.ColorError)
76			return contentStyle.Render(errorStyle.Render(theme.IconError + " Error: " + m.error))
77		}
78	
79		return m.renderTable()
80	}
81	
82	// renderTable renders the table content
83	func (m Model) renderTable() string {
84		return m.table.View()
85	}
86	
87	// GetFooterHeight returns the footer height for this view (Rule 124).
88	func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
89		switch m.mode {
90		case ModeSelecting:
91			return 3 // tab bar + empty line + info line (mirrors RenderFooter in ModeSelecting)
92		case ModeNormal:
93			if len(m.table.Items()) > 0 && m.error == "" {
94				// filter bar (when visible) + breadcrumb tab bar + empty line + info line
95				return 3 + m.table.FilterBar().ExtraHeight()
96			}
97		}
98		return 2 // empty line + info line
99	}
100	
101	// RenderFooter returns the footer content rendered below the viewport (Rule 124).
102	func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
103		if m.mode == ModeSelecting {
104			infoLine := m.footer.View(width, sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.selectionMessage})
105			return m.renderTabBar() + "\n" + theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "\n" + infoLine
106		}
107		if m.mode == ModeNormal && len(m.table.Items()) > 0 && m.error == "" {
108			var parts []string
109			if bar := m.table.FilterBar(); bar.IsVisible() {
110				parts = append(parts, bar.View())
111			}
112			parts = append(parts, m.renderTabBar(), theme.EmptyLineBg(width), m.renderInfoLine(width))
113			return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
114		}
115		// An empty listing, or one that failed to load, still gets its info line:
116		// Rule 124 budgets one whatever it holds, and this branch used to render a
117		// second blank line instead — so a footer message posted here was
118		// swallowed. That is exactly where a refusal lands (Y on an empty listing
119		// has nothing to copy), and a refusal nobody can read is worse than none.
120		return theme.EmptyLineBg(width) + "\n" + m.renderInfoLine(width)
121	}
122	
123	// renderInfoLine is the footer's one line of state.
124	//
125	// A sync's progress is read from the run rather than from footerInfo because a
126	// batch outlives the three seconds a footer message gets: a line set when the
127	// first repository started would clear while the tenth was still fetching. An
128	// error still wins over it — it is the thing that needs answering.
129	func (m Model) renderInfoLine(width int) string {
130		return m.footer.View(width, sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.jobsStatusLine(), Spinner: m.anyWorking()})
131	}
132	
133	// renderTabBar renders the breadcrumb tab bar at the bottom of the viewport
134	func (m Model) renderTabBar() string {
135		tabs := []theme.TabItem{{Label: theme.IconHome + " home"}}
136	
137		// Add navigation stack entries as tabs
138		for _, path := range m.navigationStack {
139			tabs = append(tabs, theme.TabItem{Label: theme.IconDirectory + " " + pathBaseName(path)})
140		}
141	
142		// Add current directory as last tab (if not at root)
143		if m.currentPath != "" {
144			tabs = append(tabs, theme.TabItem{Label: theme.IconDirectory + " " + pathBaseName(m.currentPath)})
145		}
146	
147		return theme.PadWithBg(theme.Bg(" ")+theme.RenderTabs(tabs, m.activeTabIndex), m.width)
148	}
149	
150	// pathBaseName returns the last component of a filesystem path.
151	//
152	// It splits with filepath, not on "/". The paths here are the ones os.ReadDir
153	// and filepath.Join produced, so on Windows they are separated by backslashes —
154	// and a split on "/" alone found nothing to cut, leaving the breadcrumb reading
155	// `󰉋 C:\Users\anthoni\workspaces\anthnell  󰉋 C:\Users\anthoni\workspaces\anthnell\devsecops`
156	// instead of `󰉋 anthnell  󰉋 devsecops`. Three tabs of that overflow the line
157	// and say less than one word each would.
158	func pathBaseName(path string) string {
159		if path == "" {
160			return ""
161		}
162		return filepath.Base(path)
163	}
164	
165	// formatGitStatus formats the git status column for a table row
166	func formatGitStatus(entry Entry) string {
167		if entry.GitBranch == "" {
168			if !entry.IsDir {
169				return ""
170			}
171			return ""
172		}
173	
174		var parts []string
175		parts = append(parts, theme.IconGitBranch+" "+entry.GitBranch)
176	
177		if entry.GitModified > 0 {
178			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", theme.IconGitModified, entry.GitModified))
179		}
180		if entry.GitUntracked > 0 {
181			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", theme.IconGitUntracked, entry.GitUntracked))
182		}
183		if entry.GitUnpushed > 0 {
184			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", theme.IconGitUnpushed, entry.GitUnpushed))
185		}
186		if entry.GitUnpulled > 0 {
187			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", theme.IconGitUnpulled, entry.GitUnpulled))
188		}
189	
190		return strings.Join(parts, " ")
191	}
192	
193	// entryIcon is the glyph in the leftmost column: what this row *is*.
194	//
195	// It replaced a Type column that showed a *project* type — detectProjectType
196	// looked for go.mod or package.json and answered "this is a Go project", which
197	// is a different question and was judged not worth a column of its own.
198	//
199	// Three genres, and the first is the one that earns the column. Half the keys
200	// in this view act on IsGitRepo — S, F, A, D, enter — and Rule 130 shows or
201	// hides them accordingly, so the user watched the shortcuts change with nothing
202	// on the row saying why. Git Status betrays a repository only when it has a
203	// readable branch: one in detached HEAD, one that is empty, one git refuses to
204	// read all showed an empty cell and looked like any other directory.
205	//
206	// A directory holding *nested* repositories still reads as a plain directory.
207	// S, F and A act on it too, so a fourth glyph would be defensible; three is
208	// what was asked for, and the row already has no other way to say it either.
209	func entryIcon(entry Entry) string {
210		switch {
211		case entry.IsGitRepo:
212			return theme.IconGitBranch
213		case entry.IsDir:
214			return theme.IconDirectory
215		default:
216			return fileicon.For(entry.Name)
217		}
218	}
219	
220	// entryIconRole colours the glyph above, and it splits the listing exactly
221	// where the row's *actions* split (availability.go): a repository can be
222	// scanned, synced and opened on its forge; a directory can be entered; a file
223	// can be read and nothing else.
224	//
225	// It is deliberately three roles and not one per file type. A per-language
226	// tint is what eza does, and it would be decoration here: what changes between
227	// two rows of this table is which shortcuts are lit, and `.go` versus `.rs`
228	// changes none of them. The colour says what the row *is for*.
229	func entryIconRole(entry Entry) theme.IconRole {
230		switch {
231		case entry.IsGitRepo:
232			// The same role the explorer paints a forge repository with. One
233			// colour for a repository across the three views that list one.
234			return theme.IconRoleRepository
235		case entry.IsDir:
236			return theme.IconRoleDirectory
237		default:
238			return theme.IconRoleFile
239		}
240	}
241	
242	// formatScanColumns returns the SENSITIVE, C, H, M, L, SCANNED column values for an entry.
243	// For git repos: looks up the scan cache directly.
244	// For directories: aggregates sub-repo scan entries.
245	func (m *Model) formatScanColumns(entry Entry, frame string) (sensitive secretsCell, c, h, med, l, scanned string) {
246		dash := "-"
247		empty := ""
248		none := secretsCell{}
249		unscanned := secretsCell{Text: dash}
250	
251		if entry.IsGitRepo {
252			if m.scanning(entry.Path) {
253				return none, dash, dash, dash, dash, frame + " scanning"
254			}
255			scanEntry, ok := m.scanCache[entry.Path]
256			if !ok {
257				return unscanned, dash, dash, dash, dash, dash
258			}
259			return secretsFor(theme.SecretsVerdict(scanEntry.Sensitive, true)),
260				fmt.Sprintf("%d", scanEntry.Critical),
261				fmt.Sprintf("%d", scanEntry.High),
262				fmt.Sprintf("%d", scanEntry.Medium),
263				fmt.Sprintf("%d", scanEntry.Low),
264				theme.IconPending + " " + timeAgo(scanEntry.ScannedAt)
265		}
266	
267		// Files are not scannable — return empty columns
268		if !entry.IsDir {
269			return none, empty, empty, empty, empty, empty
270		}
271	
272		// Directory: aggregate sub-repos
273		if len(entry.SubRepoPaths) == 0 {
274			return secretsFor(theme.SecretsUnknown), empty, empty, empty, empty, empty
275		}
276	
277		// Count how many sub-repos are currently scanning
278		scanningCount := 0
279		for _, repoPath := range entry.SubRepoPaths {
280			if m.scanning(repoPath) {
281				scanningCount++
282			}
283		}
284	
285		var scannedEntries []cache.WorkspaceScanEntry
286		for _, repoPath := range entry.SubRepoPaths {
287			if e, ok := m.scanCache[repoPath]; ok {
288				scannedEntries = append(scannedEntries, e)
289			}
290		}
291	
292		if scanningCount == 0 && len(scannedEntries) == 0 {
293			return unscanned, empty, empty, empty, empty, dash
294		}
295		// A directory with a scan running under it spins, and stops counting.
296		//
297		// It used to print "3/12" while the batch ran, incremented once per
298		// repository — a counter in a six-cell column, at the far right of a row
299		// the user is not looking at, for a batch whose progress belongs in the
300		// footer. Worse, it was the same cell that says how much of the tree has
301		// *ever* been scanned, so the two readings were indistinguishable: 3/12
302		// meant "nine left to go" or "nine nobody has scanned", depending on
303		// something the cell did not say.
304		//
305		// Now N/M means one thing — settled coverage — and the batch reports in the
306		// footer, where a batch belongs (D9).
307		if scanningCount > 0 {
308			return none, dash, dash, dash, dash, frame + " scanning"
309		}
310	
311		totalC, totalH, totalM, totalL := 0, 0, 0, 0
312		verdicts := make([]theme.SecretsState, 0, len(scannedEntries))
313		for _, e := range scannedEntries {
314			totalC += e.Critical
315			totalH += e.High
316			totalM += e.Medium
317			totalL += e.Low
318			verdicts = append(verdicts, theme.SecretsVerdict(e.Sensitive, true))
319		}
320	
321		scannedCount := len(scannedEntries)
322		totalCount := len(entry.SubRepoPaths)
323		scanned = theme.IconDirectory + " " + fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", scannedCount, totalCount)
324	
325		// The directory only carries the scanned repositories: the ones that are
326		// not enter the verdict through the count below, not through a verdict
327		// of their own.
328		if scannedCount < totalCount {
329			verdicts = append(verdicts, theme.SecretsUnknown)
330		}
331	
332		return secretsFor(foldSecrets(verdicts)),
333			fmt.Sprintf("%d", totalC),
334			fmt.Sprintf("%d", totalH),
335			fmt.Sprintf("%d", totalM),
336			fmt.Sprintf("%d", totalL),
337			scanned
338	}
339	
340	// ciCellFor is the CI grade of one row.
341	//
342	// **Only a repository is graded.** A directory aggregates its sub-repositories
343	// for the severity counters, because counts add up; letters do not — the worst
344	// of three grades is not the grade of anything, and an average is arithmetic on
345	// a scale that has none. So a directory shows nothing rather than a number
346	// nobody could act on.
347	//
348	// A repository whose remote is not this context's forge is *unavailable* rather
349	// than *never scanned*: a dash means "not yet", and this one never will be from
350	// here (§3.42). The two absences are told apart by the state, never by the
351	// printed cell.
352	func (m *Model) ciCellFor(entry Entry) ciCell {
353		if !entry.IsGitRepo {
354			return ciCell{State: theme.CIScoreUnavailable}
355		}
356		// GitRemoteURL, not GitRemote: the latter is the display path the Remote
357		// column shows (`anthnel/devdesk`), which carries no host at all — a test
358		// caught it reading every repository as ungradeable.
359		gradeable := git.SameHost(entry.GitRemoteURL, m.config.Forge.URL)
360		scanEntry, scanned := m.scanCache[entry.Path]
361		if !scanned {
362			return ciCell{State: theme.CIScoreVerdict(nil, false, gradeable)}
363		}
364		return ciCell{
365			State: theme.CIScoreVerdict(scanEntry.CIScore, true, gradeable),
366			Score: scanEntry.CIScore,
367		}
368	}
369	
370	// secretsCell is the Secrets column's two halves: what it prints, and the
371	// verdict that colours it.
372	//
373	// The two are not derived from one another. The text has cases the verdict
374	// does not — a dash for a repository never scanned, nothing at all for a
375	// file, nothing either during a scan — and those three color the same way,
376	// dim, because they all say "no verdict".
377	type secretsCell struct {
378		Text  string
379		State theme.SecretsState
380	}
381	
382	// secretsFor is the cell of a target that has a verdict. Plain text
383	// (Rule 122): the color goes through Style.
384	func secretsFor(state theme.SecretsState) secretsCell {
385		return secretsCell{Text: theme.SecretsIcon(state), State: state}
386	}
387	
388	// foldSecrets is the verdict a directory row carries for the repositories under
389	// it. A found secret outranks everything; a repository nobody looked at
390	// outranks "clean", because a parent cannot be more certain than what is
391	// unknown about its children.
392	func foldSecrets(states []theme.SecretsState) theme.SecretsState {
393		out := theme.SecretsClean
394		if len(states) == 0 {
395			return theme.SecretsUnknown
396		}
397		for _, state := range states {
398			switch state {
399			case theme.SecretsFound:
400				return theme.SecretsFound
401			case theme.SecretsUnknown:
402				out = theme.SecretsUnknown
403			}
404		}
405		return out
406	}
407	
408	// timeAgo is a local alias for theme.TimeAgo (Rule 127).
409	func timeAgo(t time.Time) string { return theme.TimeAgo(t) }
410	
411	// HeaderView interface implementation
412	
413	func (m Model) GetShortcuts() shortcut.Shortcuts {
414		// Mode input
415		if m.mode == ModeAdding {
416			return []shortcut.Shortcut{
417				{Key: "enter", Description: "Create"},
418				{Key: "esc", Description: "Cancel"},
419			}
420		}
421	
422		// Mode renaming
423		if m.mode == ModeRenaming {
424			return []shortcut.Shortcut{
425				{Key: "enter", Description: "Rename"},
426				{Key: "esc", Description: "Cancel"},
427			}
428		}
429	
430		// Mode confirm
431		if m.mode == ModeConfirmingDelete {
432			return []shortcut.Shortcut{
433				{Key: "y/n", Description: "Confirm"},
434				{Key: "esc", Description: "Cancel"},
435			}
436		}
437	
438		// Selection mode
439		if m.mode == ModeSelecting {
440			return []shortcut.Shortcut{
441				{Key: "←→", Description: "Open/Back"},
442				{Key: "enter", Description: "Select"},
443				{Key: "esc", Description: "Back/Cancel"},
444			}
445		}
446	
447		// Normal mode — every action of this mode is listed, in one order, and the
448		// ones that do not apply to the current row are greyed out (Rule 130).
449		//
450		// The key sequence is therefore the same on every row: this column is read
451		// out of the corner of the eye, and one that re-orders itself as the cursor
452		// moves cannot be. What varies is Disabled, plus enter's wording — it opens
453		// a file in the viewer and a scanned repository's findings, which are two
454		// actions that cannot both apply.
455		a := m.actions()
456	
457		enterDescription := "Scan details"
458		if entry, ok := m.selectedEntry(); ok && !entry.IsDir {
459			enterDescription = "View file"
460		}
461	
462		return []shortcut.Shortcut{
463			{Key: "←→", Description: "Open/Back"},
464			{Key: "enter", Description: enterDescription, Disabled: !a.Enter.Enabled()},
465			{Key: keymap.Terminal, Description: "Terminal"},
466			{Key: keymap.IDE, Description: "IDE"},
467			{Key: keymap.Web, Description: "Browser", Disabled: !a.Web.Enabled()},
468			{Key: keymap.Scan, Description: "Scan", Disabled: !a.Scan.Enabled()},
469			{Key: keymap.Fetch, Description: "Sync", Disabled: !a.Sync.Enabled()},
470			{Key: keymap.ScanAll, Description: "Scan all", Disabled: !a.All.Enabled()},
471			{Key: keymap.New, Description: "New directory"},

1	// Package keymap declares the application's keyboard vocabulary.
2	//
3	// It does not read any key and does not depend on bubbletea: it is a list of
4	// strings, and its only role is to be the reference the tests check the code
5	// against (keymap_test.go). Without this reference, key consistency is a
6	// convention that nothing verifies — which is exactly the state §3.26 found:
7	// 184 bindings, 16 collisions.
8	//
9	// # Three disjoint namespaces
10	//
11	//   - An UPPERCASE letter is an action, and its meaning is global to the
12	//     application. `D` deletes, in every view, whatever "delete" means
13	//     wherever you are.
14	//   - A lowercase letter is a filter or a display toggle. It changes
15	//     nothing, so its meaning can be local and two views can use the same
16	//     letter without contradicting each other.
17	//   - Everything else (arrows, esc, enter, tab, space, `/`, `.`, `?`, `:`) is
18	//     structural and never changes.
19	//
20	// # Why Shift carries the actions
21	//
22	// This isn't a matter of taste, it's the real budget of a terminal:
23	//
24	//	Ctrl+letter  : only encodes ASCII 0x40-0x5F, and the tty confiscates
25	//	               four of them (ctrl+i = TAB, ctrl+m = Enter, ctrl+j = LF,
26	//	               ctrl+h = Backspace). ctrl+a and ctrl+b are screen's and
27	//	               tmux's prefixes, ctrl+c/ctrl+d are SIGINT and EOF,
28	//	               ctrl+s/ctrl+q are flow control.           → ~14 left
29	//	Alt+key      : Option is not Meta on macOS unless the user enables it;
30	//	               the application receives nothing.                → 0
31	//	Ctrl+Shift   : the control code erases case — ctrl+a and ctrl+shift+a
32	//	               both emit 0x01. Telling them apart requires the Kitty
33	//	               keyboard protocol or modifyOtherKeys, which bubbletea
34	//	               v1.3.10 does not enable (that's WithKeyboardEnhancements()
35	//	               in v2). And even then the emulator claims them first:
36	//	               ctrl+shift+c/v/t/w/n are copy, paste, tab, close, window.
37	//	                                                                  → 0
38	//	Shift+letter : no constraint. Works on every emulator, every platform,
39	//	               through SSH and tmux.                             → 26
40	//
41	// Shift+letter IS a two-key combination: two fingers, no accidental firing.
42	// It carries the vocabulary not by default, but because the two other
43	// families are crippled or unusable.
44	package keymap
45	
46	import (
47		"maps"
48		"sort"
49		"strings"
50	)
51	
52	// The 23 actions. About forty actions used to exist for 26 letters: the
53	// rule only holds after merging synonyms (Kill = stop and kill,
54	// Delete = delete and remove, Terminal = terminal and shell) and because
55	// display toggles are excluded from the count.
56	const (
57		New      = "N" // Create a resource from this context
58		Edit     = "E" // Edit the selected resource
59		Delete   = "D" // Delete the selected resource
60		Rename   = "M" // Rename (mv)
61		Scan     = "S" // Scan the selected target
62		ScanAll  = "A" // Scan everything (modal: "purge the cache first" checkbox)
63		Fetch    = "F" // Catch up with the source: fetch + fast-forward, or follow a stream
64		Clone    = "C" // Enter clone selection
65		Terminal = "T" // Open a terminal or shell
66		IDE      = "O" // Open in the configured IDE
67		Web      = "W" // Open a URL in the browser
68		Logs     = "L" // Open the logs
69		Pager    = "V" // Open in the system pager
70		Kill     = "K" // Stop, kill (modal: Stop / Restart, or SIGKILL)
71		Prune    = "P" // Remove unused resources
72		Browser  = "B" // Open the multi-registry browser
73		Get      = "G" // Pull (get) the image or tag
74		Auth     = "U" // Login / logout of the registry — toggles based on the row's state
75		Exclude  = "X" // Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore
76		Requests = "R" // Open merge requests · PRs
77		Issues   = "I" // Open issues
78		Diagnose = "H" // Open network diagnostics on this target
79		// Copy is `Y` — yank. The letter was free even though a modal uses it
80		// for "Yes": a modal claims every key before the view sees it, so the
81		// two are never reachable at the same time.
82		Copy = "Y" // Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard — a path, or a document's content
83	)
84	
85	// CommandMode opens the command line, from anywhere — including from a
86	// focused text field.
87	//
88	// ctrl+p, and not ctrl+: : ":" is 0x3A, outside the 0x40-0x5F range Ctrl
89	// encodes, so "ctrl+:" never reaches the application. The fallback was
90	// alt+:, which has the opposite flaw: on Terminal.app and iTerm2,
91	// Option+Shift+; emits a literal character and the key doesn't arrive
92	// either. ctrl+p is free throughout the application, is not a tty control
93	// character, is not the prefix of any multiplexer, and its meaning is
94	// already learned — command palette.
95	const CommandMode = "ctrl+p"
96	
97	// actions maps each action key to its meaning. This is the table the tests
98	// check the code against; the table in §3.26 is its readable form.
99	var actions = map[string]string{
100		New:      "Create a resource from this context",
101		Edit:     "Edit the selected resource",
102		Delete:   "Delete the selected resource",
103		Rename:   "Rename",
104		Scan:     "Scan the selected target",
105		ScanAll:  "Scan everything",
106		Fetch:    "Catch up with the source",
107		Clone:    "Enter clone selection",
108		Terminal: "Open a terminal or shell",
109		IDE:      "Open in the configured IDE",
110		Web:      "Open a URL in the browser",
111		Logs:     "Open the logs",
112		Pager:    "Open in the system pager",
113		Kill:     "Stop or kill",
114		Prune:    "Remove unused resources",
115		Browser:  "Open the multi-registry browser",
116		Get:      "Pull the image or tag",
117		Auth:     "Log in or out of the registry",
118		Exclude:  "Exclude — add to .gitleaksignore",
119		Requests: "Open merge requests · PRs",
120		Issues:   "Open issues",
121		Diagnose: "Open network diagnostics on this target",
122		Copy:     "Copy the obvious thing to the clipboard",
123	}
124	
125	// Actions returns a copy of the key → meaning table.
126	func Actions() map[string]string {
127		out := make(map[string]string, len(actions))
128		maps.Copy(out, actions)
129		return out
130	}
131	
132	// IsAction reports whether a key belongs to the action vocabulary.
133	func IsAction(key string) bool {
134		_, ok := actions[key]
135		return ok
136	}
137	
138	// modalKeys are the shortcuts of a confirmation modal.
139	//
140	// This is a fourth namespace, and it is disjoint from the other three by
141	// mode rather than by case: a modal claims every key before the view sees
142	// it (priority 1 in every handleKeyMsg), so `N` cannot mean "create" there
143	// — the view underneath receives nothing. Same argument as for InEditMode.
144	//
145	// They are declared here because the §3.26 survey had not seen them, and
146	// an uppercase letter bound without a declaration is indistinguishable
147	// from drift.
148	var modalKeys = map[string]string{
149		"y": "Yes", "Y": "Yes",
150		"n": "No", "N": "No",
151	}
152	
153	// ModalKeys returns the modal shortcuts.
154	func ModalKeys() map[string]string {
155		out := make(map[string]string, len(modalKeys))
156		maps.Copy(out, modalKeys)
157		return out
158	}
159	
160	// IsModalKey reports whether a key is a modal shortcut.
161	func IsModalKey(key string) bool {
162		_, ok := modalKeys[key]
163		return ok
164	}
165	
166	// free lists the uppercase letters no action occupies. They are declared
167	// rather than left to be inferred: the next addition must know where to
168	// pick from without redoing the survey, and an action that settles
169	// somewhere other than here is a duplicate that goes unnoticed.
170	// H came back here with §3.47 (it used to trace the route, removed because
171	// it answered for the Docker VM rather than for the machine, D57) and left
172	// again with Diagnose (§3.66): a good semantic fit for "look closer at this
173	// target's network path." A letter an action has just freed up is
174	// re-declared free, otherwise it stays reserved for a use that no longer
175	// exists.
176	var free = []string{"J", "Q", "Z"}
177	
178	// Free returns the still-available uppercase letters, sorted.
179	func Free() []string {
180		out := append([]string(nil), free...)
181		sort.Strings(out)
182		return out
183	}
184	
185	// Surface is a screen, its files, and the lowercase letters it uses.
186	//
187	// Path is what ties a file to its surface, and it is there so the
188	// declaration is checkable: without it, "these letters are local to this
189	// view" is verified by merging every list, and `l` declared for netdiag
190	// would excuse `l` in the registries. Matching is done on the longest
191	// prefix, so netdiag/ports can narrow down netdiag.
192	type Surface struct {
193		Name string
194		Path string
195		Keys []string
196	}
197	
198	// localToggles inventories the lowercase letters used as display or filter
199	// toggles. They change nothing, so their meaning is local and the same
200	// letter can serve twice without contradiction — `l` is the protocol in
201	// netdiag and the LOW severity in security.
202	//
203	// A file that matches no surface is entitled to no lowercase letter at
204	// all: that is the default, and it is what makes the list worth keeping
205	// up to date.
206	var localToggles = []Surface{
207		{"containers", "ui/containers/", []string{"r", "p", "s", "t", "z"}},
208		{"viewer", "ui/viewer/", []string{"f", "c", "w", "v", "t", "n", "g", "s"}},
209		{"netdiag/ports", "ui/netdiag/ports_model.go", []string{"t", "u", "l", "e", "n", "z"}},
210		{"netdiag/checks", "ui/netdiag/", []string{"p"}},
211		{"oci/browser", "ui/oci_resources/browser_", []string{"r"}},
212		{"security/findings", "ui/security/", []string{"c", "h", "m", "l"}},
213	}
214	
215	// LocalToggles returns the declared surfaces.
216	func LocalToggles() []Surface {
217		return append([]Surface(nil), localToggles...)
218	}
219	
220	// SurfaceFor ties a file path to its surface, by longest prefix. The
221	// second return says whether a surface was found.
222	func SurfaceFor(path string) (Surface, bool) {
223		var best Surface
224		found := false
225		for _, s := range localToggles {
226			if !strings.Contains(path, s.Path) {
227				continue
228			}
229			if !found || len(s.Path) > len(best.Path) {
230				best, found = s, true
231			}
232		}
233		return best, found
234	}
235	
236	// Exception is a key that deviates from the vocabulary, with its reason.
237	type Exception struct {
238		Key     string
239		Surface string
240		Why     string
241	}
242	
243	// exceptions are the two accepted deviations. They are written here
244	// because §3.26 requires it: an undeclared exception is indistinguishable
245	// from drift, and the next survey would "fix" it.
246	var exceptions = []Exception{
247		{
248			Key:     "o",
249			Surface: "security/results/ci-tab",
250			Why: "Ouvrir le pipeline résolu par le forge. Même raison que `c` : " +
251				"l'action n'existe que sur un onglet, et brûler une des trois " +
252				"dernières majuscules libres pour ça coûterait plus que ça ne " +
253				"rapporte. `o` plutôt qu'une autre lettre parce qu'il veut déjà " +
254				"dire « ouvrir ce que cet écran désigne » dans l'état détail de " +
255				"la même vue, où il ouvre la référence d'un finding.",
256		},
257		{
258			Key:     "ctrl+y",
259			Surface: "oci/launch-form",
260			Why: "Copier la commande docker run. Même raison, et ctrl+y ne heurte " +
261				"aucun caractère de contrôle utilisé ailleurs.",
262		},
263	}
264	
265	// DeclaredExceptions returns the declared exceptions.
266	func DeclaredExceptions() []Exception {
267		return append([]Exception(nil), exceptions...)
268	}
269	
270	// IsException reports whether a key is a declared exception on a surface.
271	func IsException(key string) bool {
272		for _, e := range exceptions {
273			if e.Key == key {
274				return true
275			}
276		}
277		return false
278	}

# Fuzzy-find navigation in the Workspaces view (`g`)

## Context

The `ws` view is a single-level drill-down browser: reaching a directory
nested several levels deep means repeatedly pressing `→` and reading each
intermediate listing. There is no way to jump straight to a known
subdirectory by name. This plan adds a fuzzy-find prompt, opened with `g`:
type a few characters, get a ranked list of matching directories anywhere
under the workspaces root, move through it, and press `Enter` to land in
that directory's parent listing with the matched directory's row selected
— i.e. "back in tree mode, positioned on the node," per the request.

Confirmed with the user:
- **Trigger**: lowercase `g`. Uppercase `G` already means "Pull (get)"
  globally (`internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go:73`, used today in
  `internal/ui/oci_resources`) and reusing it for a different, view-local
  meaning would violate Rule 111's "one uppercase letter, one meaning
  everywhere" invariant even though it would pass the mechanical lint
  (`IsAction("G")` is already true). `g` mirrors an existing, identical
  precedent: the document viewer's `g` opens a "go to line" prompt that
  takes an argument, declared as a local toggle for that surface
  (`keymap.go:208`, `internal/ui/viewer/goto.go`) rather than as a global
  action. The same mechanism is reused here — no new `exceptions` entry,
  just a new `Surface` row.
- **Scope**: the whole workspaces root, walked fresh every time `g` opens
  — not just the currently browsed subtree.
- **Targets**: directories only, not files.

One derived design decision, stated explicitly since it wasn't asked
directly: the recursive walk **stops descending once it finds a git
repository**, exactly like the existing nested-repo discovery
(`detectSubRepos`/`walkSubRepos`, `internal/ui/workspaces/entry.go:112-195`).
A repository is still a valid, matchable fuzzy-find target — you can land
on it — but its internal tree (`.git`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, build
output) is never walked. This mirrors the existing, documented rationale
("a repository's own node_modules or vendor tree is never entered") and
keeps the walk's cost bounded the same way `detectSubRepos` already is on
this codebase (measured 283ms worst case over the Go module cache). Since
`ws` itself *does* let you drill manually into a repo's contents, this is
a deliberate trade-off (breadth of matchable targets vs. walk cost) worth
flagging in review, but it keeps this feature's performance in the same
ballpark as an operation already accepted in this view.

## Current architecture (relevant facts)

- `ws` has **no in-memory tree** — `Model.currentPath` /
  `navigationStack` / `cursorStack` describe one listing at a time;
  `loadEntries()` (`internal/ui/workspaces/table.go:61-126`) reads exactly
  one directory per navigation step (`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go:38-49`).
- Mode switches follow one consistent shape throughout this package: a
  `ViewMode` enum value, a component pointer field on `Model`, a branch at
  the top of `handleKeyMsg` (`update.go:194-280`) that delegates to the
  component while that mode is active, a matching branch in `View()`
  (`view.go:29-80`), and mode-aware `GetShortcuts()` /
  `GetFooterHeight()` / `RenderFooter()`. `startAdd()` /`ModeAdding`
  (`update.go:404-409`) is the closest precedent for "a component that
  owns its own key handling while a mode flag is set."
- The existing `/` filter (`components.FilterBar`, wired through
  `datatable.Model`) is a **live substring filter over the single
  directory currently loaded** — a different feature (narrows what's
  already on screen) from a **cross-tree fuzzy search that changes what's
  loaded**. It is not reused as a mechanism, only as a UI/visual precedent
  (a bar, `esc` cancels, `enter` confirms).
- No fuzzy-matching code or dependency exists anywhere in this repo — the
  scorer is new code.
- `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` is the single source of truth checked by
  AST-scanning tests (`internal/ui/keymap/keymap_test.go`,
  `announced_test.go`). A new lowercase binding must appear in
  `localToggles` for a `Surface` matching the file path, or
  `TestEveryLowercaseBindingIsDeclared` fails.

## Design

### 1. Keymap registration

Add a `Surface` entry in `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go`'s `localToggles`
(`keymap.go:206-213`):

```go
{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
```

`ws` currently declares no local lowercase toggles, so this is a new row,
not an addition to an existing one.

### 2. New mode and model fields

`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go`:
- New `ViewMode` value `ModeFuzzyFinding`.
- New field `fuzzyFinder *FuzzyFinder` (mirrors `input *WorkspaceInput`).
- New field `pendingSelectPath string` — parallel to the existing
  `pendingCursor int` (`model.go:48`), but selects a row **by absolute
  path** once a freshly-loaded listing lands, rather than by index. Needed

on it — but its internal tree (`.git`, `vendor/`, `node_modules/`, build
output) is never walked. This mirrors the existing, documented rationale
("a repository's own node_modules or vendor tree is never entered") and
keeps the walk's cost bounded the same way `detectSubRepos` already is on
this codebase (measured 283ms worst case over the Go module cache). Since
`ws` itself *does* let you drill manually into a repo's contents, this is
a deliberate trade-off (breadth of matchable targets vs. walk cost) worth
flagging in review, but it keeps this feature's performance in the same
ballpark as an operation already accepted in this view.

## Current architecture (relevant facts)

- `ws` has **no in-memory tree** — `Model.currentPath` /
  `navigationStack` / `cursorStack` describe one listing at a time;
  `loadEntries()` (`internal/ui/workspaces/table.go:61-126`) reads exactly
  one directory per navigation step (`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go:38-49`).
- Mode switches follow one consistent shape throughout this package: a
  `ViewMode` enum value, a component pointer field on `Model`, a branch at
  the top of `handleKeyMsg` (`update.go:194-280`) that delegates to the
  component while that mode is active, a matching branch in `View()`
  (`view.go:29-80`), and mode-aware `GetShortcuts()` /
  `GetFooterHeight()` / `RenderFooter()`. `startAdd()` /`ModeAdding`
  (`update.go:404-409`) is the closest precedent for "a component that
  owns its own key handling while a mode flag is set."
- The existing `/` filter (`components.FilterBar`, wired through
  `datatable.Model`) is a **live substring filter over the single
  directory currently loaded** — a different feature (narrows what's
  already on screen) from a **cross-tree fuzzy search that changes what's
  loaded**. It is not reused as a mechanism, only as a UI/visual precedent
  (a bar, `esc` cancels, `enter` confirms).
- No fuzzy-matching code or dependency exists anywhere in this repo — the
  scorer is new code.
- `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` is the single source of truth checked by
  AST-scanning tests (`internal/ui/keymap/keymap_test.go`,
  `announced_test.go`). A new lowercase binding must appear in
  `localToggles` for a `Surface` matching the file path, or
  `TestEveryLowercaseBindingIsDeclared` fails.

## Design

### 1. Keymap registration

Add a `Surface` entry in `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go`'s `localToggles`
(`keymap.go:206-213`):

```go
{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}},
```

`ws` currently declares no local lowercase toggles, so this is a new row,
not an addition to an existing one.

### 2. New mode and model fields

`internal/ui/workspaces/model.go`:
- New `ViewMode` value `ModeFuzzyFinding`.
- New field `fuzzyFinder *FuzzyFinder` (mirrors `input *WorkspaceInput`).
- New field `pendingSelectPath string` — parallel to the existing
  `pendingCursor int` (`model.go:48`), but selects a row **by absolute
  path** once a freshly-loaded listing lands, rather than by index. Needed
  because after a jump we know the target's path but not its position in
  the not-yet-loaded listing.

### 3. Recursive directory walk (new file, e.g. `fuzzywalk.go`)

A function collecting every directory path under the workspaces root,
pruned at repository boundaries, sharing the existing hidden-file
(`isHidden`, `entry.go:22-24`) and symlink-cycle-safety logic
(`mayFollow`, `leadsToDir`, `entry.go:196-268`) that `walkSubRepos` already
implements. Concretely: refactor `walkSubRepos`
(`internal/ui/workspaces/entry.go:145-195`) so the "stop at a repo /
follow-or-skip a link" traversal is shared between the existing
repo-only collector and a new all-directories collector — e.g. a shared
recursive helper parameterized by what it records at each directory
(repo root only, vs. every directory), rather than a second, independently
written walk that must re-derive the same cycle-guard correctness.

Runs as a `tea.Cmd` (never inline in `Update`, per Rule 110), returning a
new message, e.g. `FuzzyPathsLoadedMsg{Paths []string, Skipped int}`. Kicked
off immediately when `g` is pressed (`startFuzzyFind()`), not per
keystroke — so results are typically ready before the user has typed 3
characters. `Paths` are stored relative to the workspaces root (matching
against a clean `a/b/c`-style string, not an absolute machine path).

### 4. Fuzzy scorer (new file, e.g. `fuzzymatch.go`)

A small, self-contained, pure function (no dependency exists to reuse):
subsequence match (query characters must appear in order, case-insensitive)
over each candidate relative path, producing a score that favors
consecutive runs and matches starting at a path-segment boundary (after
`/`). Returns non-matches as "no match" so the caller filters them out.
Pure and easily table-driven-tested in isolation.

### 5. `FuzzyFinder` component (new file, e.g. `fuzzyfind.go`)

Owns: a `textinput.Model` for the typed query, the full path list once
loaded (`loading bool` until `FuzzyPathsLoadedMsg` arrives), and a
`datatable.Model[fuzzyRow]` used purely for rendering + cursor movement
over the **already-ranked** result list (`fuzzyRow{ Path string }`, one
`SizingContent` column, `Less: nil`/`SortColumn: -1` — the component
computes and re-sorts by score itself on every query change and calls
`SetItems`, rather than delegating ranking to the table). This keeps
`ws`'s existing per-table styling (Rule 106/116/122) instead of a bespoke
render, at the cost of not using the table's own sort/filter features
(deliberately unused here — the order is the scorer's, not the user's).

Behavior:
- Below 3 typed characters: show a neutral prompt state, no query run
  (matches the request's "au-delà de trois").
- 3+ characters: filter+rank the loaded path list, `SetItems` on the
  inner table.
- `↑↓`/`pgup`/`pgdown`/`home`/`end`: forwarded to the inner
  `datatable.Model`.
- `Esc`: returns a new `FuzzyFindCancelMsg{}`.
- `Enter` on a selected row: returns a new `FuzzyFindConfirmMsg{Path string}`.
- Anything else: forwarded to the `textinput.Model`.

`GetHeaderInfo`/footer status text (e.g. "Type at least 3 characters" /
"N matches" / a loading spinner while the walk is still in flight) is
exposed via a small method the parent's `RenderFooter` reads, mirroring
the existing `m.jobsStatusLine()`/`m.anyWorking()` pattern
(`view.go:129-131`) rather than owning its own footer rendering.

Rendered full-viewport by the parent (`View()` returns
`m.fuzzyFinder.View()` while `ModeFuzzyFinding` is active) rather than as
a centered `lipgloss.Place` overlay like `ModeAdding`/`ModeRenaming` — a
ranked result list needs real vertical space, and this is what Rule 112
actually asks for (full-viewport, not modal), even though this package's
two existing form modes use the modal pattern instead. Worth flagging as
a deliberate choice, not a copy of the nearest precedent in this file.

### 6. Wiring into `Model.Update` / `handleKeyMsg`

`update.go`:
- `handleKeyMsg`: new priority branch (same position as the other mode
  checks, before the `ModeNormal` switch) delegating to
  `m.fuzzyFinder.Update(msg)` while `ModeFuzzyFinding`.
- `ModeNormal` switch (`update.go:239-277`): new `case "g":` →
  `m.startFuzzyFind()`, which sets `mode = ModeFuzzyFinding`, builds
  `fuzzyFinder = NewFuzzyFinder()`, and returns the path-walk `Cmd`.
- Top-level `Update`'s message switch gets three new cases:
  - `FuzzyPathsLoadedMsg`: stores the paths on `m.fuzzyFinder` and lets it
    recompute if a query is already typed (mutation happens here, in
    `Update`, per Rule 110 — not inside the `Cmd`).
  - `FuzzyFindCancelMsg`: `mode = ModeNormal`, `fuzzyFinder = nil`.
  - `FuzzyFindConfirmMsg{Path}`: `mode = ModeNormal`, `fuzzyFinder = nil`,
    then `m.jumpToPath(msg.Path)`.

### 7. `jumpToPath` — synthesizing drill-down state (new, in `update.go` or a new file)

Pure, testable logic computing what `navigateIn()` would have built had
the user manually drilled down to the target's parent, then requesting a
load with a pending by-path selection:

- `parent := filepath.Dir(target)`.
- If `parent == workspacesRoot`: `currentPath = ""`, `navigationStack = nil`.
- Else: walk `parent` upward to the root collecting each ancestor;
  `currentPath` = the immediate parent (deepest ancestor), `navigationStack`
  = the remaining ancestors in shallow-to-deep order (mirrors exactly what
  `navigateIn`'s `append(m.navigationStack, m.currentPath)` builds one
  step at a time — see `update.go:319-339`).
- `cursorStack` reset to zero-valued entries (one per `navigationStack`
  level) — there is no real prior cursor history for levels the user never
  actually browsed through.
- `pendingSelectPath = target`, `activeTabIndex = tabCount()-1`.
- Returns `m, m.loadEntries()`.

Then a small addition to the existing `EntriesLoadedMsg` handler
(`update.go:55-74`): after `m.setEntries(...)`, if `pendingSelectPath !=
""`, look it up among `m.entries()` (existing helper, `table.go:41-47`)
and `m.table.SetCursor(idx)` if found, then clear the field — parallel to,
and independent of, the existing index-based `pendingCursor` restoration
right below it.

### 8. Header/footer/help plumbing

- `view.go` `GetShortcuts()`: new `ModeFuzzyFinding` branch —
  `{Key: "enter", Description: "Select"}`, `{Key: "esc", Description:
  "Cancel"}` (↑↓ omitted per Rule 138 — universal navigation).
- `GetFooterHeight()`/`RenderFooter()`: new `ModeFuzzyFinding` case,
  2-line footer showing the finder's status text (loading / prompt /
  match count) via the existing `m.footer` component.
- `GetHelpContent()`: one new `KeyBinding` entry for `g`, and a short new
  `Section` describing the feature (3-character minimum, whole-tree scope,
  directories only, lands on the matched node).

## Files touched

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` | add `{"workspaces", "ui/workspaces/", []string{"g"}}` to `localToggles` |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/entry.go` | refactor `walkSubRepos` to share its traversal with the new all-directories collector |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/fuzzywalk.go` *(new)* | recursive directory collector, pruned at repo boundaries |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/fuzzymatch.go` *(new)* | subsequence fuzzy scorer, pure function |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/fuzzyfind.go` *(new)* | `FuzzyFinder` component: query input, ranked results, key handling, `View()` |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/model.go` | `ModeFuzzyFinding`, `fuzzyFinder` field, `pendingSelectPath` field |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/update.go` | `startFuzzyFind`, `jumpToPath`, new message cases, `EntriesLoadedMsg` by-path selection, `case "g":` |
| `internal/ui/workspaces/view.go` | `View()` branch, `GetShortcuts()`, `GetFooterHeight()`/`RenderFooter()`, `GetHelpContent()` |

## Verification

- New unit tests, table-driven (per repo convention):
  - `fuzzymatch_test.go` — scorer: matches/rejects, ordering by score.
  - `jumpToPath`-equivalent pure function — ancestor-chain construction for
    root-level, one-level, and multi-level nested targets.
  - `fuzzywalk_test.go` — collector against a small temp directory tree:
    confirms it does not descend into a repo's own contents, follows the
    existing hidden-file setting, and matches `detectSubRepos`'s
    symlink-cycle safety (can reuse the same test fixtures/style as
    `entry_test.go` if one exists — check before writing new fixtures).
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/ui/workspaces/...` (and
  `./internal/ui/keymap/...`, since `keymap_test.go` AST-scans the new
  `case "g":`/`localToggles` entry).
- `golangci-lint run` and `mise run check` before considering this done
  (Rule 301/305).
- Manual verification in the running TUI (`mise run dev`): press `g` in
  `ws`, confirm no results below 3 characters, type a query matching a
  known nested directory, move through results, press `Enter`, confirm the
  breadcrumb and selected row land exactly on that directory. Also verify
  `Esc` cancels back to the previous listing unchanged, and that `/`
  (filter bar) and `g` don't interfere with each other.

1	package workspaces
2	
3	import (
4		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
5	
6		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/datatable"
7		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
8	)
9	
10	// Column fixed widths for the workspace table.
11	// colGitFixed: icon(1) + " "(1) + branch(~20) + up to 3 indicators × (icon+count+space)(4) = 28
12	const (
13		colNameMin        = 16
14		colGitFixed       = 28
15		colSensitiveFixed = 7
16		colCFixed         = 4
17		colHFixed         = 4
18		colMFixed         = 4
19		colLFixed         = 4
20		colScannedFixed   = 14
21		colModFixed       = 15
22		colRemoteMin      = 10
23		// colCIFixed is four cells for one letter. The title is what costs: "CI
24		// Score" is eight to show an A, which is exactly why the four severity
25		// columns are called C H M L. A fifth counting column beside them inherits
26		// their convention rather than opening a second one.
27		colCIFixed = 4
28	)
29	
30	// workspaceRow is one line of the table: the entry, plus the six scan cells.
31	// Those depend on the scan cache, on what is currently scanning and on the
32	// spinner frame — none of which lives on an Entry, and none of which the
33	// columns can reach, since they are built once in New. Same shape as
34	// oci_resources' imageRow, and for the same reason.
35	type workspaceRow struct {
36		Entry Entry
37		// GitStatus is the branch and its counts, or the spinner while a sync is
38		// rewriting exactly those counts. Showing the stale numbers under a
39		// spinner elsewhere in the row would be showing the state being replaced.
40		GitStatus string
41		Sensitive secretsCell
42		CI        ciCell
43		Critical  string
44		High      string
45		Medium    string
46		Low       string
47		Scanned   string
48	}
49	
50	// workspaceColumns describes the workspaces table. Nothing sorts: the order is
51	// the directory's, and `.` stays inert rather than being wired to a comparator
52	// no one asked for. Name and Remote are what the filter has always matched.
53	// ciColumn is the CI grade. It exists only when scan.enable_ci_score is on:
54	// off, it would be four cells of nothing on every row for the life of the view,
55	// which says less than no column at all. The setting is read at construction
56	// and the router drops this view on a save, so the column follows.
57	//
58	// It does **not** declare Optional. Its four states include two absences that
59	// mean different things, and a column that disappeared when the terminal got
60	// narrow would add a third — "not shown" — indistinguishable from the other
61	// two. Fewer columns that are right beats every column wrong (§3.45), and this
62	// one is a verdict rather than a detail.
63	func ciColumn() datatable.Column[workspaceRow] {
64		return datatable.Column[workspaceRow]{
65			Title: "CI", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: colCIFixed,
66			Cell:  func(r workspaceRow) string { return theme.CIScoreCell(r.CI.State, r.CI.Score) },
67			Style: func(r workspaceRow) lipgloss.Style { return theme.CIScoreStyle(r.CI.State, r.CI.Score) },
68		}
69	}
70	
71	// ciCell is what the column prints and what decides its colour, kept apart so
72	// the colour is never read back off the rendered string — which is what the
73	// Secrets column used to do and what had to be undone.
74	type ciCell struct {
75		State theme.CIScoreState
76		Score *string
77	}
78	
79	func workspaceColumns(withCI bool) []datatable.Column[workspaceRow] {
80		text := func(title string, width int, cell func(workspaceRow) string) datatable.Column[workspaceRow] {
81			return datatable.Column[workspaceRow]{Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, Optional: true, MinWidth: width, Cell: cell}
82		}
83		cols := []datatable.Column[workspaceRow]{
84			{
85				// No title: the column carries a glyph, and a header over it would
86				// name something the user reads at a glance anyway — eza does not
87				// print one either. It declares neither Less nor Search: it adds no
88				// text anyone could type, so the filter stays on Name and Remote.
89				Title: "", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: datatable.IconColumnWidth,
90				Cell:  func(r workspaceRow) string { return entryIcon(r.Entry) },
91				Style: func(r workspaceRow) lipgloss.Style { return theme.IconStyle(entryIconRole(r.Entry)) },
92			},
93			{
94				Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: colNameMin,
95				Cell:   func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Entry.Name },
96				Search: func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Entry.Name },
97			},
98			{
99				Title: "Remote", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, TruncateHead: true, MinWidth: colRemoteMin, Flex: 1,
100				Cell:   func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Entry.GitRemote },
101				Search: func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Entry.GitRemote },
102			},
103			{
104				Title: "Git Status", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: colGitFixed,
105				Cell:  func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.GitStatus },
106				Style: gitStatusStyle,
107			},
108			{
109				Title: "Secrets", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: colSensitiveFixed,
110				Cell:  func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Sensitive.Text },
111				Style: func(r workspaceRow) lipgloss.Style { return theme.SecretsStyle(r.Sensitive.State) },
112			},
113			count("C", "CRITICAL", colCFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Critical }),
114			count("H", "HIGH", colHFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.High }),
115			count("M", "MEDIUM", colMFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Medium }),
116			count("L", "LOW", colLFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Low }),
117			text("Scanned", colScannedFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return r.Scanned }),
118			text("Modified", colModFixed, func(r workspaceRow) string { return timeAgo(r.Entry.ModTime) }),
119		}
120		if withCI {
121			// Beside the four severity counters, which is where a reader looks for
122			// what a scan concluded — not at the end, past Scanned and Modified.
123			cols = append(cols[:len(cols)-2], append([]datatable.Column[workspaceRow]{ciColumn()}, cols[len(cols)-2:]...)...)
124		}
125		return cols
126	}
127	
128	// count builds one of the four severity columns. The cell is already formatted
129	// by formatScanColumns, so the colour is decided from what it printed: "-" for
130	// a repository never scanned, "" for something that cannot be, and a number
131	// otherwise.
132	//
133	// Only a non-zero count is coloured. A clean repository showing four coloured
134	// zeroes reads as four problems at a glance, which is the opposite of what the
135	// colour is for.
136	func count(title, severity string, width int, cell func(workspaceRow) string) datatable.Column[workspaceRow] {
137		return datatable.Column[workspaceRow]{
138			Title: title, Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: width,
139			Cell: cell,
140			Style: func(r workspaceRow) lipgloss.Style {
141				switch cell(r) {
142				case "", "-", "0":
143					return theme.DimStyle
144				}
145				return theme.SeverityTextStyle(severity)
146			},
147		}
148	}
149	
150	// gitStatusStyle warns when the working tree holds work that is not committed.
151	//
152	// It is the same condition `s` refuses to sync on, so the colour says in
153	// advance what the sync would have reported: a repository with uncommitted
154	// changes is skipped, untracked files included.
155	func gitStatusStyle(r workspaceRow) lipgloss.Style {
156		switch {
157		case r.Entry.GitBranch == "":
158			return theme.DimStyle
159		case r.Entry.GitModified > 0 || r.Entry.GitUntracked > 0:
160			return theme.StatusWarningStyle
161		}
162		// No opinion here: the table sets the theme's text color.
163		return lipgloss.NewStyle()
164	}
165	
166	// rowsFor decorates the entries with the scan state the table shows.
167	func (m *Model) rowsFor(entries []Entry) []workspaceRow {
168		frame := m.jobFrame
169	
170		rows := make([]workspaceRow, 0, len(entries))
171		for _, entry := range entries {
172			sensitive, c, h, med, l, scanned := m.formatScanColumns(entry, frame)
173			gitStatus := formatGitStatus(entry)
174			// A row can only be held by one of the two — busy() is what keeps them
175			// apart — so the order below decides nothing. The delete spends this
176			// cell for the same reason the sync does, and with less to lose: a
177			// directory on its way out has no git status left to announce.
178			switch {
179			case m.deleting(entry.Path):
180				gitStatus = frame + " deleting"
181			case m.syncing(entry.Path):
182				gitStatus = frame + " syncing"
183			}
184			rows = append(rows, workspaceRow{

1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
30		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
31		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
32		"github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
33	
34		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
35		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
36	)
37	
38	// Sizing is what decides a column's width: the number it declared, or the
39	// content it holds. Every column states one — the zero value is refused by
40	// TestEveryColumnDeclaresItsSizing rather than given a meaning, because a
41	// default here would decide for twenty tables nobody had looked at (D12).
42	type Sizing int
43	
44	const (
45		// SizingUnset is the zero value, and means nothing. See the test above.
46		SizingUnset Sizing = iota
47		// SizingFixed takes exactly the width declared. For a count, a state, an
48		// icon — anything whose size was known when the code was written.
49		SizingFixed
50		// SizingContent takes the width of its widest visible value, never below
51		// MinWidth and never above MaxWidth. For paths, URLs, addresses, image
52		// references: values whose length is a property of the data.
53		SizingContent
54	)
55	
56	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
57	type Column[T any] struct {
58		Title string
59		// Sizing is the column's nature (see above). It has no default.
60		Sizing Sizing
61		// MinWidth is the width a SizingFixed column takes, and the floor a
62		// SizingContent column is never squeezed under.
63		//
64		// It is a floor now, not the request it used to be: the shortfall comes out
65		// of the content columns down to their MinWidth, and after that whole
66		// columns are removed rather than emptied one cell at a time (widths.go).
67		// The name stays MinWidth on a fixed column, where it *is* the width, for
68		// the reason §3.45 gives: Width would be false on a content column that
69		// grows past it, where MinWidth is merely redundant on a fixed one — a
70		// redundant name is bearable, a false one is not.
71		MinWidth int
72		// MaxWidth caps a SizingContent column. 0 means no ceiling, and there is no
73		// global default: a ceiling chosen once would apply to columns nobody has
74		// looked at, and a full IPv6 address is 45 cells — so the first "reasonable"
75		// default re-truncates exactly what the measurement was for. Meaningless on
76		// SizingFixed, where MinWidth already is the width.
77		MaxWidth int
78		// Optional marks a column that may be dropped whole when the table does not
79		// fit, before any column that is not. Orthogonal to Sizing because all four
80		// combinations exist: the interface error counters have an exact width and
81		// are also the first thing worth losing.
82		Optional bool
83		// DropFirst moves an Optional column to the head of the queue: it goes
84		// before every other Optional one, wherever it sits on screen. Meaningless
85		// without Optional, which is the flag that decides whether a column may go
86		// at all.
87		//
88		// It exists because drop() reads the column order as an order of
89		// importance, and that is true of every column whose place is chosen by
90		// what it *is*. A gauge's place is chosen by what it *illustrates* — it has
91		// to sit beside the number it draws, in the middle of the table, or it
92		// stops being read as that number's picture (§3.71). Left to position
93		// alone, the containers table would shed its I/O counters to keep two bars
94		// that are the most expendable thing on the row.
95		//
96		// A bool rather than a rank: two tiers is what the case needs, and an int
97		// would invite every table to number its columns against each other.
98		DropFirst bool
99		// TruncateHead cuts the start of an over-long value rather than its end.
100		//
101		// A flag per column rather than a rule derived from Sizing, because the
102		// answer depends on the column and not on its nature: a URL, an image
103		// reference and a path share their prefix and are told apart by their end,
104		// while an address is identified by the network it starts with. It cannot
105		// be left to Cell either — Cell does not know the width it will be rendered
106		// at, and that is deliberate: it is what makes the value measurable.
107		TruncateHead bool
108		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over once every column has
109		// what it wants. 0 takes no part; the leftover is split between the
110		// flexible ones by weight.
111		//
112		// Flex says who receives the surplus, never who needs it — which is why it
113		// cannot decide widths on its own: the ports table gave Process 110 cells
114		// for "svchost.exe" at 200 columns while Peer Address stayed frozen at 26,
115		// cutting an IPv6 endpoint in half. That is what Sizing answers.
116		Flex int
117		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: it is measured
118		// and truncated before anything is applied to it, and runewidth counts an
119		// escape sequence's bytes as width — a styled string is cut mid-escape and
120		// bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122). Taking a string rather than a
121		// styled value is what makes that unexpressible here.
122		//
123		// It must be pure and cheap. The rendering calls it once per visible cell;
124		// the measurement calls it once per cell of every visible row, off screen
125		// included. Nothing can check that — it is an arbitrary closure — so it is
126		// stated here rather than tested.
127		Cell func(T) string
128		// Style colours the cell after it has been measured and truncated, which is
129		// the only order in which colour is safe (see render.go). Nil leaves the
130		// cell in the table's own colours.
131		//
132		// On a row a view has coloured whole via SelectedStyles (error, busy, a CVE
133		// severity), it is not consulted: that row is handed to styles.Selected
134		// whole, and a colour inside it would end the highlight mid-row. On the
135		// plain "normal" selection it *is* consulted — see render.go's cellStyle,
136		// which repaints the shared background on every cell instead of once on an
137		// outer wrap, so per-cell colour and the highlight no longer fight.
138		Style func(T) lipgloss.Style
139		// Cut and TailStyle split a cell into two coloured runs instead of Style's
140		// one: Style colours the first Cut(item) cells of the *finished* text —
141		// already measured, truncated and padded to the column's width — and
142		// TailStyle colours the rest. Both nil (the ordinary case, every column but
143		// the containers load gauges) leaves Style covering the whole cell as
144		// before.
145		//
146		// This is not the gradient Rule 122 forbids: nothing styled is ever
147		// measured. Cut reads a plain, already-final string — the split happens
148		// after truncation, at the same point Style already does its colouring —
149		// so it is the same "measure first, colour after" order applied twice
150		// instead of once, not an exception to it. It stays two runs rather than an
151		// arbitrary list: one caller has needed it since it was added, and Cut, a
152		// bare integer, is cheaper to reason about than a slice of spans that only
153		// ever holds two elements.
154		//
155		// Dropped only for a row a view has coloured whole — error, busy, a CVE
156		// severity — for the same reason Style is: a two-run cell still needs its
157		// own reset between the runs, which that solid background cannot afford.
158		// The plain "normal" selection consults both: each run repaints
159		// ColorTableLineSelected and bold itself, the same per-cell repaint that makes a
160		// single-run selected cell safe, so a load gauge keeps its fill/track
161		// split under the cursor instead of collapsing to Style's colour alone.
162		Cut       func(T) int
163		TailStyle func(T) lipgloss.Style
164		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
165		// `.` skips it.
166		Less func(a, b T) bool
167		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
168		// not participate.
169		Search func(T) string
170	}
171	
172	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
173	type Config[T any] struct {
174		Columns []Column[T]
175		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
176		Tokens []components.FilterToken
177		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
178		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
179		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
180		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
181		SortColumn int
182		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
183		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
184		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
185		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
186		SortDesc bool
187		// Key identifies an item across rebuilds, and is what the busy set is held
188		// on. Nil switches the busy facility off entirely, which is the default:
189		// most tables have no action to run on a row.
190		//
191		// It cannot be a `Busy func(T) bool` on this struct instead. Columns are
192		// built once, in New, and close over nothing — imageRow exists because of
193		// that — so a predicate here would have to close over the view's map of
194		// in-flight actions, which is the same trap. Separating the identity from
195		// the state is what avoids it, and it is also what lets IsBusy answer for an
196		// object whose row does not exist yet: the guard on a confirm path runs
197		// before anything is rebuilt.
198		//
199		// Keying on identity rather than a flag on the row is also what survives the
200		// periodic refresh, which replaces the items while an action is running.
201		Key func(T) string
202		// StatusColumn is the column whose cell the spinner replaces while a row is
203		// busy — the one that answers "what about this row". Ignored when Key is
204		// nil.
205		//
206		// That column must not be sortable: askFor reserves width(Title)+2 for a
207		// column carrying a Less, which is expensive for a glyph.
208		StatusColumn int
209		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
210		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
211		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
212		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
213		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
214		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
215	}
216	
217	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
218	type Model[T any] struct {
219		cfg   Config[T]
220		table table.Model
221		bar   components.FilterBar
222	
223		items []T
224		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
225		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
226		// ordering while the screen shows another.
227		visible []T
228	
229		// styles is what was last handed to the table. The rendering is this
230		// package's now (render.go) and bubbles keeps its copy unexported, so the
231		// styles have to be kept on this side to be readable at render time.
232		styles table.Styles
233		// preserveColumnColors is true when styles.Selected is the plain "normal"
234		// look (ColorTableLineSelected) rather than a view's own error/busy/severity
235		// override. Computed once in applyStyles, read per cell in cellStyle: it
236		// is what tells the two selected-row treatments apart without render.go
237		// having to know what a severity or a busy row is.
238		preserveColumnColors bool
239		// offset is the first visible row — the scroll window bubbles kept in its
240		// viewport. clampOffset owns it.
241		offset int
242	
243		// busy maps an item's Key to the label of the action running on it. Held
244		// here rather than in the view so that one answer — IsBusy — serves the
245		// rendering, the footer and the guard that stops a second command being
246		// issued for the same object.
247		busy map[string]string
248		// spinnerFrame is what a busy row's status cell shows. The frame lives here
249		// and the tick stays in the view: a spinner needs a Cmd, and this package
250		// returns none (Rule 110).
251		spinnerFrame string
252		spinnerIdx   int
253	
254		// natural is the widest text each column produces over the visible rows,
255		// header included. rebuild refreshes it because it is already walking every
256		// cell there; it costs one lipgloss.Width per cell and nothing else.
257		natural []int
258		// measured is the copy the solver reads — natural as of the last
259		// measurement *moment*. The two are separate because the moment is the
260		// whole design: SetItems cannot tell a periodic refresh from a change of
261		// population (both arrive the same way), and remeasuring on every tick
262		// would make the columns dance on their own. See Remeasure.
263		measured []int
264		// measuredOnce records that a non-empty population has been measured. The
265		// first one measures itself: without that a table stays at its MinWidths
266		// for the life of the view, and nothing on screen says why.
267		measuredOnce bool
268	
269		sortColumn int
270		sortDesc   bool
271		width      int
272	}
273	
274	// New builds a table from its configuration.
275	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
276		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
277		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
278			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
279		}
280		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
281	
282		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
283		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
284			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
285		}
286	
287		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
288		// A frame from the start: a table whose view never calls AdvanceSpinner —
289		// one rendered in the same frame the action began — would otherwise show an
290		// empty status cell, which reads as "nothing is happening".
291		m.AdvanceSpinner()
292		// Through setStyles rather than the table alone: a table rendered before
293		// anything calls applyStyles — one built and drawn in the same frame — would
294		// otherwise render with the zero Styles, which carries no cell padding and
295		// so lays out two cells narrower per column than every width was solved for.
296		m.setStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
297		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
298		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
299		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
300		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
301		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
302			m.sortColumn = -1
303			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
304			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
305			m.sortDesc = false
306		}
307		return m
308	}
309	
310	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
311	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
312	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
313	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
314	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
315		m.items = items
316		m.rebuild()
317		// The one measurement this package takes on its own initiative. Every other
318		// SetItems may be a two-second refresh, and a table that re-measured on
319		// those would reshuffle its own columns while the user reads it.
320		if !m.measuredOnce && len(m.visible) > 0 {
321			m.Remeasure()
322		}
323	}
324	
325	// Remeasure re-reads the widest value in each column and lays the table out
326	// again. Call it at the moments a *user* changed what the table holds — a tab
327	// change, a drill-down, an explicit refresh — and never on a timer.
328	//
329	// This package cannot tell those apart on its own: a periodic reload and a
330	// change of population both arrive through SetItems, so the view is the only
